name: OpenRouter rankings (token volume by model and by app)
can_show: Relative token demand across models from many providers routed through one gateway; switching between models over time; which apps drive which models; response of usage share to price changes on the same platform.
cannot_show: Total market demand or first-party API traffic (direct OpenAI/Anthropic/Google API calls and consumer chat apps never touch the router); revenue; enterprise contracts; usage inside China.
sampling_bias: Self-selected users: price-sensitive developers, hobbyists and agent/coding tools that want multi-model routing are over-represented; large enterprises are under-represented. | A few heavy apps (coding agents, role-play) dominate tokens; one app switching model can move a model's share by several points. Report shares with and without the top apps. | Free and promotional model variants inflate tokens for some open-weight models; keep ':free' variants as a separate flag rather than merging them silently. | Rankings show only the top-N models/apps per period; long tail is left-censored (record as missing, not zero). | Platform growth itself raises all levels; use shares or normalise by platform total. | Scraped from the site's undocumented frontend endpoints: daily data exists only for the last ~31 days and the weekly chart only for ~53 weeks x top ~9 models, so history before the first scrape is top-N only. Collect weekly to build the full series.

name: GitHub new repositories mentioning a provider SDK or endpoint
can_show: Flow of new developer projects building on each provider; timing of developer interest after launches and price cuts.
cannot_show: Production usage or spend; private/enterprise repositories; whether a mentioned SDK is actually called; model-level choice within a provider.
sampling_bias: Public repositories only; hobby, tutorial and student projects dominate counts. | Keyword search matches mentions, not imports; tune queries and audit a random sample (record precision in the query table). | OpenAI-compatible endpoints mean many non-OpenAI projects mention 'openai'; this inflates OpenAI counts. | GitHub user base grows over time; normalise by all new repos in the same month. | Search index is revised; counts for a past month can change when re-queried. Keep retrieval date.

name: PyPI downloads of provider SDK packages
can_show: Installation activity for first-party SDKs (openai, anthropic, google-genai, mistralai, ...); trend and relative growth across providers.
cannot_show: Distinct users or projects; spend; model-level demand; usage through raw HTTP or OpenAI-compatible SDKs pointed at other providers.
sampling_bias: Dominated by CI pipelines and container builds, not people; levels are not users. | The 'openai' package is used to call many other providers via compatible endpoints. | Mirror traffic excluded (pypistats without_mirrors); version bumps cause re-install spikes. | pypistats API keeps only ~180 days; longer history needs the BigQuery public dataset.

name: npm downloads of provider SDK packages
can_show: JavaScript/TypeScript SDK installation activity; complements PyPI for web apps.
cannot_show: Same limits as PyPI: not users, not spend, not model choice.
sampling_bias: CI and bundler installs dominate; dependency of popular frameworks drives counts. | Scoped packages (@anthropic-ai/sdk, @google/genai) were renamed over time; chain old and new package names in the package map.

name: Hugging Face downloads and derivatives of open-weight models
can_show: Demand for self-hosted open weights (downloads, likes, number of fine-tunes); the outside option to paid APIs; Chinese open-weight models' global uptake.
cannot_show: Inference volume after download; closed models; downloads via mirrors (ModelScope, hf-mirror) or other hosts; historical values before collection started (API returns only rolling 30-day and all-time totals).
sampling_bias: One download = one file fetch by any client, incl. CI and re-downloads; not users. | Quantised re-uploads by third parties split demand across repos; aggregate via the crosswalk's base model, keep repo-level too. | No history from the API: a panel exists only from the first snapshot. Schedule collection weekly; derive period flows from all-time differences. | Chinese users often download from ModelScope; HF under-counts CN demand.

name: Provider disclosures: filings, earnings calls, official blog/keynote statements
can_show: Absolute scale: tokens processed, AI revenue run-rate, API vs. consumer split, customer and developer counts. Anchors the relative measures to levels.
cannot_show: Model-level or price-tier detail; consistent definitions over time; anything a firm chooses not to disclose (selection on good news).
sampling_bias: Unaudited and strategically timed: firms disclose when numbers look good. | Definitions drift (monthly vs. daily tokens, run-rate vs. recognised revenue, 'developers' vs. 'customers'). Store the exact quote and unit; never harmonise silently. | Sparse: a handful of points per firm per year. Do not interpolate into the monthly panel; use as level anchors or in a separate provider x quarter panel. | Private firms (OpenAI, Anthropic) disclose via press and interviews, not filings: mark is_estimate when the figure is reported second-hand.

name: Chinese demand: public usage announcements and platform rankings
can_show: Order-of-magnitude token volumes announced by Chinese providers and cloud platforms (e.g. daily token calls at developer conferences); app-store and platform ranking positions; direction of change around domestic price cuts.
cannot_show: A comparable time series; model-level usage shares; any audited measure; usage of foreign models in China (largely unavailable).
sampling_bias: Announcement-driven: numbers appear at launches and conferences, gaps in between. | Metric definitions differ by firm (daily vs. cumulative tokens; calls vs. tokens). | Rankings are ordinal and published by parties with commercial interests. | Expect THIN coverage. The coverage report lists every model x month cell with no Chinese demand data; thesis text must state these gaps rather than impute them.

name: Official adoption surveys and job postings
can_show: Economy-wide adoption rates (e.g. statistical-office business surveys) and labour demand for provider-specific skills; used to check that platform-based measures track broader adoption.
cannot_show: Model choice or price response; anything at weekly frequency.
sampling_bias: Survey frames, questions and waves differ by country and year. | Job-posting keyword counts reflect hiring cycles and posting practices, not usage.
